doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His parents: schoolteacher mother and well-regarded father
summary: Panken and Audre sketch his mother's arrival in Tippo and his father's reputation for decent treatment of Black neighbors.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But a lot happened between those events, and I’d like to discuss that if we can. Here’s what I know from the interviews, and just tell me whatever you can, however you can flesh it out. First of all, we’ve only been talking about your father here, but your mom was a schoolteacher, I gather.
Yes.
Do you know what grades she taught?
She taught 3rd and 4th grade, I think, at Tippo Elementary. We didn’t like the... They had the school, and they would teach 6th and 7th grade or something like that...
Your mother was not really happy with the school.
Yeah.
It was a tiny little building. Because there was hardly anyone who lived around there.
Well, I don’t remember it being a tiny little building.
It looked tiny to me.
I guess it’s all relative. You’re from St. Louis originally.
Yes.
There’s an oral history with your mother on the internet, which I came across yesterday, and I figured it had to be your mother. She said she came to Tippo in 1926.
I don’t know...
She saw an advertisement that said the position paid $150 a month, which is why she went to Tippo. But when she got there, she found out it only paid $100 a month.
Yeah.
In any event, she arrived in 1926, she met your father, they were married in February of ‘27 and you were born in November of ‘27.
[LAUGHS]
What was your father like and what was your mother like?
My father was well known around the area. He was an exemplary... He was known as somebody that was nice to the blacks. He dealt with them...
I remember that he put plumbing into the manager’s house, and a lot of people around there thought that was a bold move, that they might have to do the same or something like that.
Oh, well...I don’t know...
He was really highly regarded. In that BBC documentary, one of the old black

men who had been manager on the farm talks about him. They put up a sign in Tippo a long time ago, not the historical marker, but a tin sign that said, “Mose Allison was born here,” and he said, “That should have said ‘Mose Allison, Senior, was born here.’”
Yes.
So your dad had a really good reputation.
So he was an enlightened man.
Yeah.
